column1: # Orbital phase zero points and longitudes of periastron, read by hand from the
# literature. One row per system. Neither quantity is in F23, so neither can be
# derived: every value here is a reading of a published paper, and the quote
# column carries the sentence or table row it was read from, so any entry can
# be checked against its source without re-reading the paper.
# MJD_T0    the epoch, converted to MJD where the paper gives JD or HJD
# e_MJD_T0  its uncertainty in days, the larger side when asymmetric
# T0_kind   what the epoch is, in the paper's own terms. Values used:
#             Tpi/2                 mean longitude 90 deg; superior conjunction
#                                   of the compact object when e = 0
#             mid-eclipse           centre of the X-ray eclipse
#             ellipsoidal minimum   optical minimum, i.e. a conjunction
#             outburst              an outburst maximum or first detection
#             folding origin        an arbitrary origin used to fold a light
# omega_deg longitude (argument) of periastron, degrees, as published
# omega_frame whose orbit omega describes: `compact` when it comes from pulse
#           timing of the X-ray source (the paper quotes a_X sin i in light
#           seconds) or from the compact object's own lines, `donor` when it
#           comes from radial velocities of the companion (the paper quotes K1
#           or a1 sin i of the star). The two differ by exactly 180 degrees.
